claims.text: The initial alloy is a multiphase refractory high-entropy alloy produced by conventional casting.
The as-cast alloy has a homogeneous solid solution with minimal precipitate content.
A controlled post-casting thermo-mechanical treatment can promote uniform precipitation of coherent nanoscale Laves-phase particles.
Annealing temperature and time can be optimized to nucleate and grow uniformly distributed coherent Laves-phase nanoprecipitates.
A modest increase in Nb content relative to the other elements may favor Laves-phase precipitation.
The treatment produces nanoscale coherent Laves-phase precipitates uniformly distributed in the alloy matrix.
The Laves-phase nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion through precipitation strengthening.
Coherence between the precipitates and matrix minimizes stress concentrations.
Preserving grain-boundary integrity maintains thermal stability and resistance to irradiation-induced damage.
The treatment will improve yield strength relative to the as-cast, unprocessed alloy.
The treatment will improve creep resistance relative to the as-cast, unprocessed alloy.
The mechanical-property improvement may be approximately 20% relative to the as-cast, unprocessed baseline.
The treated alloy will maintain phase stability and irradiation durability.
The benefits are expected under operating temperatures of at least 1000 °C and under irradiation exposure.
The intervention is expected to work only for compositions and annealing conditions that produce coherent nanoscale precipitates.
Coarse or incoherent precipitates caused by overtreatment or unfavorable composition may eliminate the anticipated benefits.
The magnitude of strengthening depends on precipitation kinetics and irradiation conditions.
Extreme irradiation may create a tradeoff between precipitation strengthening and embrittlement.

contradictions.description: The initial alloy is described as both multiphase and a homogeneous solid solution, without explaining whether the homogeneous solid solution is only the matrix or how multiple phases are present.
The hypothesis specifies a thermo-mechanical treatment, but the intervention and experiment describe annealing without a defined mechanical-deformation step.
